title: Paul's thoughts, another's wording
english: After other remarks he adds this: I, speaking my opinion, would say that the thoughts are the Apostle's, but the wording and the composition belong to someone who recorded the apostolic teaching and, as it were, wrote notes on what was said by the teacher."

orientation: Origen is giving his own opinion about who composed the Epistle to the Hebrews, after noting that its style is more polished than Paul's.

title: The church that holds Hebrews as Paul's may be approved, but only God knows the writer
english: Origen continues: So if any church holds this Epistle as Paul's, let it be approved even in this, for the ancients did not hand it down as Paul's without reason. But who wrote the Epistle, the truth God knows.

orientation: Origen has just given his own opinion that the thoughts are Paul's but the wording and composition are by a recorder of the apostle's teaching; now he turns to the church's reception of the epistle and the hidden identity of its actual writer.

title: The tradition that reached us about the epistle's writer
english: The tradition that has come down to us says that some claim Clement of Rome, who became bishop of the Romans, wrote the Epistle, while others claim it was Luke, the one who wrote the Gospel and Acts.
